Reproduced all three defects on the frozen base with a temp script: protocol fault left the kernel PID alive (orphan kept the Node event loop open), a 400ms timeout did not bound a silent ready wait, and eval after dispose still attempted a spawn (kind=spawn).

Implemented unified terminal transitions: Kernel.handleExit now always kills the process tree before onExit eviction; Kernel.waitReady races the ready promise against the effective cell timeout and the caller AbortSignal through handleExit; Kernel.dispose rejects a pending ready and marks exited; RlmRuntimeImpl is terminal after dispose so eval rejects closed without spawning; ready version mismatch was rerouted through handleExit.

limitations: The ready startup deadline reuses the effective cell timeout (input.timeout ?? config.timeout) as its own budget; startup and cell execution are not charged against one shared deadline and no separate startup-timeout option was added.

Protocol-fault coverage drives the host parser by having a cell write raw frames through sys.__stdout__; the unmodified production kernel never emits malformed frames, so these tests validate host defensive behavior only.

Reproduced the reviewer/coordinator finding on b1f13ae: on Windows child_process.spawn of a missing command returns first and then emits an unlistened async error; Kernel.kill spawned bare taskkill with no error listener. Verified with Node v24 on this host: unhandled error exits the process, a listened error surfaces ENOENT then close (-4058).

Wrote three red tests against b1f13ae before any implementation: (a) taskkill startup failure under bogus SystemRoot+PATH with guarded restore asserts no host crash and a fallback-settled kernel PID; (b) bounded startup (0.5s pressed ready) plus a slow cell under one 1200ms budget asserts total elapsed < 1600ms, PID gone and a fresh session works; (c) a late abort after a settled eval must not evict the idle kernel.

Implemented the fixes: resolveTaskkill() reads SystemRoot??C:\\Windows at kill time; killWin32() spawns the absolute path with NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1, listens error and non-zero close and falls back to child.kill() exactly once; kill() is idempotent via killStarted; RlmRuntimeImpl.eval computes one deadline and waitReady/evalCell consume the same budget; waitReady has settled/readyDone guards with synchronous cleanup in finish/finally.

Adaptation/rejection notes: adopted absolute-System32 taskkill + NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath + /T /F from the prime-agent orphan reaper but used async spawn with error/close listeners instead of its blocking spawnSync so terminal paths never block and never crash on a missing killer; kept /T /F tree semantics and pid targeting; rejected the rlm reference separate _startup_timeout (no public startupTimeout per frozen scope) and its graceful shutdown frame/daemon/sandbox cleanup (V1 keeps direct kill + fallback; no daemon, no journal, no public Kernel provider).

Ran gates before staging: red proofs on b1f13ae (taskkill run interrupted the test process; shared-deadline run measured 1881ms for a 1200ms budget), then pnpm typecheck, pnpm build, node --test tests/rlm-loop.test.ts, pnpm test and pnpm check:memory. The record is staged with the material change and the staged/range gates were validated at commit time without rewriting any existing record line.

The shared-deadline regression uses bounded wall-clock timing (0.5s pressed startup + 1.2s budget, asserting < 1.6s); deterministic on this host but still timing-sensitive under extreme CI load; no fake timers were introduced.

The resolveReady-to-finally window is provably unreachable for macrotask timer/abort events (microtasks finish before the next event); the added settled/readyDone guards are defense-in-depth and do not extend the state machine.
